text: the little robot bo spent its days in the observatory on the hill. every morning it polished the great brass telescope until the metal sang. every evening it wrote down what the stars had told it in a blue notebook. the stars were patient teachers and bo was a careful student. one night a comet passed close enough to warm the cold glass of the lens. bo recorded the visit in the notebook with a drawing of a long bright tail. the observatory librarian a tall quiet machine named vera read the entry twice. vera said that comets were letters that the sky sent to those who watched. bo decided to write a letter back and it worked on it for eleven nights. the letter said thank you for passing by you made the cold season bright. when the letter was done bo folded it into a paper plane of solar foil. vera launched the plane from the top of the tower during a meteor shower. the wind carried it up past the clouds and out over the dark sleeping town. bo did not know whether the comet would read the letter and it did not matter. what mattered was the writing the watching and the waiting between the two. in spring a seed of star iron landed in the observatory garden and took root. by summer it had grown into a small tree with silver leaves that hummed at dusk. bo measured the tree every day and the tree grew exactly one millimetre a night. vera said the tree was listening to the comet and repeating its song very slowly. years later travellers climbed the hill just to sit under the humming silver leaves. they asked bo what the tree was singing and bo showed them the blue notebook. on the last page under the drawing of the comet there was a single line of notes. the notes were the melody of the tree and of the comet and of the paper plane. the travellers copied the melody and carried it down into every valley of the world. and that is how a small robot a comet and a silver tree taught the world to listen.
